newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel barges bid up, low sulphur holds steady.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel barges bid up, low sulphur holds steady.

text.p: European fuel barge prices were bid up on Tuesday while low sulphur cargo values were steady, with north German barrels seen heading into Italy, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $83.25, $84.25 and $84.50 a tonne in the ARA area with better bunker demand and short covering seen the cause of the $1 rise on the previous day.
But some traders were sceptical as to the real strength in the market.
"People say there is a physical shortage but I am not convinced," said one dealer. "I believe we are at a rather artificial level."
Slim differentials between the barge market and bunker prices of around $85-$86 in Rotterdam and $87 in Antwerp underlined some of the doubts about the morning's rise.
Low sulphur cargo markets were steady, with 50,000 tonnes of north German one percent barrels heard traded to Italy via a dealer, at around current NWE swaps levels.
Low sulphur straight-run sellers were still bullish, pegging offer levels at around $109-$110 fob a tonne, citing firmer crude and tight near-term supplies.
